The same statement is already pinned by tests/unit/test_config_table_module_switches.py::test_the_two_b8b_fragments_arm_the_block_and_nothing_else, which sets the key aside by name on cell B8b's fragments so it cannot be confused with that cell's factor. harness_robustness_key.behaviour: reproduction.ojw.native_episode._finite_terminal_outcome retains the row with terminal_disposition = {reason: finite_completion, finish_reason, role_id, stage, revision_count, planner_accepted: false, rejected_contact}, records the truncated contact under interrupted_role, and delivers the latest delivery-eligible Solver draft (terminal_solver_receipt) or, when no Solver completed, an abstention with empty actor_output bound to the rejected contact. rails.native_episode_receipt.validate_native_episode_terminal_policy refuses that delivery unless the configured policy is exactly deliver-latest-or-abstain, and rails.runner refuses a disposition that differs from its actual quarantined completion.
harness_robustness_key.diagnostic: Rows whose terminal_disposition.reason is finite_completion are RETAINED and scored as delivered -- the latest delivery-eligible Solver draft, or an abstention with empty output when no Solver completed -- and are never filtered out of the paired read. Their count, their sample ids and the by-role / by-stage / by-finish-reason breakdown that analysis.native_episode_diagnostics emits as finite_stops are a MANDATORY diagnostic in the verdict. A high count is a finding about the role's output length on this base; it is reported, not repaired inside this cell.

b7a.text: ADMITTED iff the primary official SLU CI95 lower bound is > 0 against the anchor, intent is non-inferior at the own null margin 1.0051 pp, the symmetric-normalised scorer agrees in sign, and no scenario loses intent beyond the null band. NEUTRAL iff both primary metrics are non-inferior within the own null margins (SLU 1.1218, intent 1.0051); a NEUTRAL L1 still enters the SLURP default plan, because it removes a named defect class at no measured cost -- the seven malformed drafts that reached the Planner unflagged and the 2,167 unstructured reviews now carry a declared, receipted disposition. HARMFUL otherwise, and then L2 is not flown.

failure_policy: Stop and preserve on the first failure. Do not automatically restart, replay, filter rows, change the roster, role graph, prompts, geometry or caps. This registration carries its own single root-diagnosed recovery allowance, and under owner decision 22 of 2026-09-18 that recovery takes the RESUME-RECOVERY form: its own experiment fragment declaring resume_from {attempt_id, trace_sha256}, the same run id, replayed model-free by core.flight.resume so COMPLETE rows are kept without selection and only the rest are flown. A second failure closes this flight: no third registration, no replay, no row filtering, and the fix must be proven on a four-row dry run before another mechanism is admitted. A failed four-row smoke stops v2 on the same terms.

The recovery is registered as its OWN experiment fragment carrying resume_from {attempt_id, trace_sha256} under the SAME run id and a new attempt id, and the run-cumulative budget already covers predecessor plus worst case because core.attempts.AttemptStore.prior_actual_usage sums every attempt of the run id.

v1_closure.root_cause: The SLURP native baselines omit native_episode.finite_completion_policy and rails.native_episode_config.load_native_episode_config defaults it to 'raise' (raw.get("finite_completion_policy", "raise")), so one truncated completion aborts the whole campaign. The alternative 'deliver-latest-or-abstain' is already implemented and tested in the harness.
